Lithium may be used for the prophylaxis of recurrent unipolar depression as an alternative to standard antide- pressants, although it is more commonly used in the management of bipolar disorder (see above); its role in unipolar depression is more usually to augment the ef- fect of standard antidepressants in treatment-resistant disease. An area of particular concern with regard to initial choice of an antidepressant is the most appropriate drug for pa- tients considered to be a high suicide risk.15 It is important to remember that suicide is an inherent risk in depression; it is generally accepted that with all antidepressant thera- pies the risk of suicide may increase in the early stages of recovery (for further details, see Effects on Mental State, under Fluoxetine, p.392). Varying relative risks of toxicity in overdosage for different groups of antidepressant have been assessed:16-19 • older tricyclics and the tetracyclic maprotiline20 appear to be more toxic in overdosage than the tetracyclic mianserin21 and the SSRIs18,22 • MAOIs have an intermediate risk22,23 • within the tricyclic group, desipramine16,17,22 has been reported to be associated more frequently with fatal overdosage although some24 assign this status to do- sulepin. The BNF considers amitriptyline and dosulepin to be particularly dangerous in overdosage; lofepramine19,22,25 may be one of the safer tricyclics • toxicity of the SNRI venlafaxine in overdose appears to be greater than other new serotonergic antidepressants and comparable to some of the less toxic tricyclics22 Although such analyses cannot determine to what extent the data reflect prescribing patterns and patient selection as opposed to drug toxicity16,17,25 it is widely accepted that the older tricyclics are more toxic in overdosage, and that the SSRIs26,27 and the newer tricyclic and related cyclic antidepressants are safer.27 In practice, it is often difficult to identify patients at high risk for suicide, and it has there- fore been suggested that a routine strategy should be to be- gin antidepressant therapy in all patients with drugs that have low toxicity in overdose.15,27 However, whichever antidepressant is chosen, all patients should be closely monitored during early therapy until significant improve- ment in depression has been observed and limited quanti- ties of antidepressants should be prescribed at any one time.
